concept: FDE Interview Practice And Timed Mock
title: FDE 90-Minute Mock Interview
briefing: Use the original company-neutral interview practice lesson and a timer. This is not a reported employer loop. Attempt discovery, coding and design before reading reference answers; use the recruiter's actual tool rules when known. The app records a self-assessment checklist, not hiring readiness.
objectives: Clarify an ambiguous request before choosing technology.
Implement and test a scoped receipt rule and defend recovery boundaries.
Explain scope, evaluation and factual ownership under time pressure.

prediction.prompt: Which interview dimension needs the most deliberate practice?

steps.title: 0–15 minutes: clarify Northstar
steps.instructions: Ask about the user, workflow, baseline, data, permissions and exceptions. Have a peer reveal a missing access approval and conflicting resolution definitions. Write a short brief.

steps.title: 15–35 minutes: implement the receipt rule
steps.instructions: Implement tenant/request identity, replay and payload conflict in your preferred language with deterministic tests. Explain the in-memory concurrency and restart limits.

steps.title: 35–55 minutes: design and trace failure
steps.instructions: Draw the application and optional durable action path. Trace source staleness, revocation, timeout and remote success followed by a crash. Separate outbox acceptance from provider reconciliation.

steps.title: 55–70 minutes: defend delivery
steps.instructions: Propose a two-week pilot, representative evaluation, rollout and handover. Respond to added refund scope with options. Explain final-artifact startup validation.

steps.title: 70–80 minutes: ownership stories
steps.instructions: Tell one real ambiguity story and one failure story. Identify your contribution, decision, alternatives, observed result, uncertainty and lesson.

steps.title: 80–90 minutes: questions and scoring
steps.instructions: Ask role-fit questions and score discovery, coding, architecture, evaluation, communication and ownership from zero to four using the lesson rubric. Select one concrete improvement; 18/24 is a practice heuristic only.

reflectionPrompts: Which follow-up exposed your weakest assumption?
What is one test or explanation you will improve before repeating?
extensionChallenge: Repeat with a data-integration role that uses no LLM. Replace model evaluation with reconciliation and data-quality acceptance while preserving customer and operational reasoning.

evidenceChecklist.label: I clarified the user, task, constraints and success measure.
I tested identity, replay and conflicting payload behavior.
I traced uncertainty and recovery without claiming exactly-once effects.
I defended a bounded pilot and evaluation plan.
I used factual ownership stories and scored all six dimensions.
